summary: Extends the snoop packet capture file format with identifiers for additional link-layer media types. The snoop format stores network packet traces so they can be saved and exchanged between tools, and this memo adds codes for newer kinds of network links.

plainLanguage.summary: Snoop files store captured network packets and identify the link type in a header. This memo adds several link-type values and defines a registry for them.

subtitle: New link-type codes and an IANA registry for snoop packet capture files.

tldr.problem: The snoop capture format uses a Datalink Type field to identify the link type, and needed additional values.
tldr.mechanism: The memo adds codes for Fibre Channel, ATM, ATM Classical IP, and IP over Infiniband, and creates an IANA registry.
tldr.outcome: New allocations from code 27 follow First Come First Served; specified unused values through 26 are reserved.

today: RFC 3827 is an Informational memo defining snoop datalink codes and the corresponding IANA registry. The unit metadata lists no update or replacement.

sections.title: The Snoop Datalink Field
sections.content:
The snoop file format stores captured packets for tools that capture, display, and interpret network traffic. Its header contains a Datalink Type field identifying the network's datalink type.

RFC 3827 adds values for additional media and creates an IANA registry to hold snoop datalink types.
sections.plainLanguage: A packet capture file records what kind of link carried the packets. The memo expands the list of link types the file can name.

sections.title: Additional Datalink Codes
sections.content:
The RFC assigns code 16 to Fibre Channel, 17 to ATM, 18 to ATM Classical IP, and 26 to IP over Infiniband. It refers to another document for the IP over Infiniband packet format.

These are the additions defined by this RFC, alongside values previously listed in RFC 1761.
sections.plainLanguage: Four link types receive codes in this memo: Fibre Channel, ATM, ATM Classical IP, and IP over Infiniband.

sections.title: The IANA Registry
sections.content:
The new Snoop Datalink Types registry contains 32-bit (4-octet) values, including values previously defined by RFC 1761 and the additions in this document.

Allocations starting at code 27 follow First Come First Served. The memo reserves undefined values 10–15 and 19–25.
sections.plainLanguage: The IANA registry keeps the values in one place. New allocations starting at 27 use a first-come policy, while listed gaps are reserved.
